   Even though I already mentioned this, I want to reiterate it because

cannot do anything about what has already happened and we don’t know
what the future will bring. We also cannot control other players. They will
make plays at the table that will sometimes seem nonsensical. Our only
option is to focus on playing our very best, and if we want to channel

   Use systems to optimize your preparation. What’s something you

can you implement to master the strategic and mental skills that will lead
you to playing consistently well?
   You may be wondering about how to go about creating your own sys-
tems. You have many options, but you probably want to start by looking
at your action plan and desires from the last chapter. Answering the fol-
lowing questions will give you a better handle on what your systems

     ♠ What is it that you want to accomplish?
     ♠ Why do you want to achieve it? What will it mean to you?
     ♠ What’s the plan for getting there? Can you break this into small
        steps that can be carried out daily?
     ♠ Are there any likely obstacles that might crop up along the way?
        How can we deal with them?
     ♠ What is the level of difficulty of what you are trying to
        accomplish?
     ♠ Is there anyone who can help or coach you?
     ♠ What can give you energy and momentum along the way?

                                                    Systematizing Success

   If you take the time to answer these questions, you should be able to
come up with some concrete ideas for processes that you can implement
to help you achieve your poker goals.

Why Systems Fail
All of this sounds well and good but, as we all know, most people fail to fol-
low a system of goals of any sort, regularly. There are numerous reasons
why people fail to follow through on their process plans. First of all, it is
very easy to get distracted. We get pulled in lots of directions. There are
many things vying for our attention and it’s easy for the day to slip by
without us accomplishing much towards our goals. Also, if we are not really
dedicated to our plans, it’s easy to put off implementing them. To combat
this, it is important to have a clear understanding of what our most impor-
tant priorities are at any given time. If we make a list of two or three things
that we are committed to accomplishing each day and we do those things
at the top of the day, we are more likely to stick it out and progress in a
timely fashion. This is another reason why a morning routine is so impor-
tant. Also, you should conduct a review at the end of the day to assess how
it went. Did you hit any roadblocks or obstacles that kept you from your
most important tasks? Is there any way to remove them in the future?
    Another thing that can impact us negatively is discouragement. We like
it when things go smoothly, but often things do not go as planned. Maybe
we have friends and family members who are critical of what we are try-
ing to achieve. Perhaps we engage in negative self-talk. Failure is espe-
cially tough and when things aren’t going well, it is easy to give up. Re-
member, being a successful poker player is inherently difficult and not
many people make it. Sticking to a system of improvement makes it more
likely that you will succeed, so you must hang in there.
    The final reason why most people don’t stick to their goals and ideals is
because they lack desperation. Are you desperate to achieve the goals
you have set for yourself? If you don’t achieve your goal, will you be ab-
solutely crushed? How much do you want it? Take some time to reflect
on how much you want poker success. Are you willing to do the small

Peak Poker Performance

things associated with making your dream a reality? If you are not willing
to do the small things, you won’t be willing to do the large things.

Summary
Herbert Grey said it best: “Successful people focus on pleasing results and
unsuccessful people focus on pleasing methods.” In other words, if you
want to be a success, you have to be willing to step out there and do what
it takes to get those pleasing results. The unsuccessful want to do what is
easy and pleasant, which is usually staying in the comfort zone. If you want
to succeed, you are going to have to do the hard stuff every single day. If
you are willing, success is within your grasp. Everyone has to start at the
beginning and even though we usually don’t see it, the greats had to spend
the time learning the fundamentals and developing their talent. When in
doubt, ask yourself, “Is this a pro decision or an amateur decision?” Spend
most of your time making pro decisions and success will be yours.

Chapter Highlights
     ♠ A system is a specific activity you do regularly to increase your
        odds of success or happiness.
     ♠ Implementing a morning routine of a few simple endeavors can
        make it possible to take your life to the next level.
     ♠ Making small, smart choices consistently over time makes a radical
        difference.
     ♠ As making rapid, dramatic changes can be difficult, try a systems
        approach where you look for very small incremental
        improvements on the order of 5%.
     ♠ Progress accelerates when we emphasize improvement over
        perfection. By taking things slowly and creating systems that lead
        to small, incremental wins, we take the pressure for perfection off.
     ♠ Making continual improvement through kaizen is more effective
        than radical all or nothing strategies.
     ♠ Success requires hard work.

                                                   Systematizing Success

Jonathan’s Comments
I am a big believer in developing systems that make it difficult for me to
sabotage myself. Without a solid game plan, I find it quite easy to get
relatively few things accomplished in my daily life. Instead of wandering
aimlessly, I implement a large number of systems that force me to stay on
the path to success.
    For example, every morning, whether I am at home or traveling the
high stakes live tournament circuit, I wake up, drink a huge blended vege-
table smoothie, take a freezing cold shower, then meditate. This ensures I
can start my work day with a clear mind.
    Recently, when I sit down at the poker table, I turn off my phone and
resolve not to turn it on again until I am on a decently long break. This en-
sures my phone will not interrupt my train of thought. I realize that play-
ing poker is the most important thing in the world to me at that point in
my life and no phone call or email is worthy of distracting me.
    On my breaks, instead of stumbling around trying to find something to
do for 15 minutes, I go to the bathroom then find a quiet corner of the
tournament area to clear my mind. This helps rejuvenate me and helps me
stay focused on playing my best poker.
    When I am home, I keep a detailed schedule of everything I need to
work on, which lists when various projects need to be completed. Clearing
tasks off my schedule is a challenge and I derive great joy from seeing
significant projects completed. This is likely how I have managed to write
10 best-selling poker books over the last five years, despite traveling the
live poker circuit full time.
    Also while I am at home, I make a point to watch at least one hour of
poker training videos each day by studying a video while I eat lunch. Since
I eat lunch every day, this system ensures I put in some study time. As
you can see, I tie productive and healthy activities to routine tasks that
must be completed every day.
    A while back, I wrote out what my ideal, perfect day would look like.

     Chapter Four

     Deconstructing the A Game




      Flow is an optimal state of consciousness, a peak state where
      we feel our best and perform our best. It is a transformation
      available to anyone, anywhere, provided that certain initial
      considerations are met.
                                                              Steven Kotler

    You have just arrived at the table, and from the moment you sit down
you are playing unbelievably well. You are able to assess your opponents’
ranges with astounding accuracy, and often have their exact hand pegged
by the river. You can predict with near perfect accuracy how they will re-
act to bets of various sizes on each street. You are able to effortlessly
trick them into making mistakes. You are so in tune with what is going on
at the table that the money pours in.
    Having spent much time over the last few years talking with and
coaching some of the best players in the world, I can say that this is fairly
characteristic of how they describe the A game in operation. You know
you’re experiencing peak performance because everything seems to flow
perfectly. It’s as if you can do no wrong.

                                             Deconstructing the A Game

  Contrast this with statements made by players not on their A game.
They say things like:

   ♠ I wasn’t able to think through hands properly.
   ♠ I lacked focus.
   ♠ I played on autopilot without carefully analyzing situations.
   ♠ I made too many mistakes.
   ♠ I used generic hand ranges and wasn’t able to figure out how my
       opponents were playing.
   ♠ I lost more money than I needed to.
   ♠ I’m burned out.
   ♠ I was bored.

   In poker, the optimal performance state is typically referred to as the A
game. In sports it is known as being in the zone. Athletes who are in the
zone experience an optimal level of readiness that allows them to integrate
physical and mental processes in a way that leads to superior performance.
Obviously, we are not seeking an optimal physical performance when we
play poker. It is more accurate to say that in poker we are seeking an opti-
mal mental performance where we can process, integrate, and execute our
knowledge in a maximally profitable way. No matter what you call it, the
more time you can spend in an optimal performance zone, the more money
you stand to make. Top professionals differ from lesser ones in the length
of time they are capable of playing the A game. This is where the real edge
comes from when equally matched opponents play against each other.
   It’s important to understand that each person has their own personal
version of the A game. As you acquire more knowledge and skill, your
ability to exhibit your best performances will increase. As you will see in
the next section, understanding where you are in the development of
your game is a key component to developing and enhancing your A game.


                                                                         87
